title: New York Trivia Night

questions.q: Which New York City borough is also known as Kings County?
In which year did the Brooklyn Bridge open?
The Statue of Liberty was a gift to the United States from which country?
Olmsted and Vaux won an 1858 design competition with their "Greensward Plan" for which Manhattan park?
Which Major League Baseball team plays its home games in the Bronx?
What did the Dutch call their settlement on Manhattan when they founded it in the 1620s?
In the 1933 film King Kong, which skyscraper does the giant ape climb?
Which river separates Manhattan from New Jersey?
In which Manhattan square does a lit ball drop at midnight on New Year's Eve?
Which island in New York Harbor was the main federal immigration station from 1892 to 1954?

notes: Kings County is coextensive with Brooklyn; see Brooklyn Wikipedia / NY State county list
Opened 24 May 1883; see Brooklyn Bridge Wikipedia / NYC DOT
Gift of the people of France, dedicated 1886; see National Park Service Statue of Liberty page
Greensward Plan by Olmsted and Vaux, 1858; see Central Park Conservancy history
Yankee Stadium is in the Bronx; see MLB.com Yankees
New Amsterdam; briefly New Orange in 1673-74, which the 1620s date rules out.
Climax of King Kong (1933) on the Empire State Building; see AFI Catalog / film Wikipedia
Hudson River forms Manhattan's western shore; see Hudson River Wikipedia
Times Square Ball drop since 1907; see Times Square Alliance
Ellis Island immigration station operated 1892 to 1954; see National Park Service Ellis Island page
